title: Genepool — Natural Selection Lab
description: Paint a world, release founder species, and watch mutation and selection rewrite their genomes in front of you.
concept: Genepool is an agent-based evolution workbench. You design a founder genome across five genes — body size, speed, sense radius, diet and fecundity — release a colony, and let grazing, predation and starvation decide which variants persist. The world itself is editable: paint fertile soil, barren ground and water, or generate islands, floodplains and desert belts from a seed. Live charts track population, plant biomass and the drifting trait distributions, an inspector reads any individual's genome, and runs can be saved to slots, exported as CSV/JSON/PNG, or handed to someone else as a share link.
features: Five-gene founder designer with randomiser, plus mutation-rate, regrowth and population-ceiling controls
Six terrain brushes and six generators (uniform, patches, island, rivers, archipelago, desert belt) on a named seed
Six scenarios — Eden, Arms race, Island, Drought, Archipelago, Floodplain — each with its own ecology
Live population/biomass chart, selectable trait histogram and running trait averages
Click-to-inspect any organism: genome bars, generation, age, energy, clone it or copy its genes to the founder
Save slots in localStorage plus CSV history, world JSON, snapshot PNG and a state-carrying share link

interaction.mouse: Hover the world to position the brush ring; drag to paint terrain when a brush is armed.
interaction.click: With the brush off, click an organism to select it and read its genome; with Colony armed, click to drop 24 founders.
interaction.touch: Tap and drag to paint or select; the panel becomes a bottom sheet with five tabs.
interaction.keyboard: space play/pause · s step · 1/2/3 speed · r reset · c release a colony at the cursor · p snapshot PNG
